readings: Link each advanced behaviour record to its transaction (`translink` = `transreg`) and then to that transaction's trader (`trdref` = `tradereg`). Use exact text matches and drop anything without a match. For each trader type (`tradekind`), with a missing type as its own group, count the distinct transactions (`transreg`) that have behaviour records. Count each transaction once, even when two behaviour records point to it. Compute each type's share as its count divided by the total of the counts across all types. Which trader types have a share strictly above the plain average of the per-type shares? For each one, show the type, its count, its share, and its share minus the average share. Don't round anything, and return nothing if the average is missing.
queries:
WITH type_counts AS (
    SELECT t.tradekind,
           COUNT(DISTINCT tr.transreg) AS transaction_count
    FROM advancedbehavior AS ab
    JOIN transactionrecord AS tr
      ON ab.translink COLLATE BINARY = tr.transreg COLLATE BINARY
    JOIN trader AS t
      ON tr.trdref COLLATE BINARY = t.tradereg COLLATE BINARY
    GROUP BY t.tradekind
),
shares AS (
    SELECT tradekind,
           transaction_count,
           CAST(transaction_count AS REAL)
             / SUM(transaction_count) OVER () AS share
    FROM type_counts
),
average_share AS (
    SELECT AVG(share) AS value
    FROM shares
)
SELECT s.tradekind,
       s.transaction_count,
       s.share,
       s.share - a.value AS share_above_average
FROM shares AS s
CROSS JOIN average_share AS a
WHERE s.share > a.value;
